blindSummary:
A self-governing island dependency with full equality legislation including same-sex marriage (2016); historically harsh but now among the more progressive small jurisdictions; no bathroom-use restriction machinery applies.

The evidence base for this record is shared with the controlling state's entry; the local position is more protective than the controlling state's own arrangements.
blindOutOfScope: A self-governing dependency of a much larger adjacent state; local deviations are noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: an article by a public broadcaster covering a prison-housing ruling in a constituent jurisdiction of the controlling state (June 2026), not this territory; included as controlling-state context material.

NOTE: a further article by the same broadcaster on the same prison-housing litigation (Feb 2026), covering a constituent jurisdiction of the controlling state rather than this territory; context material only.

Official parliamentary report (26 April 2016): proceedings of the upper legislative chamber - third reading of the 2016 bill opening same-sex marriage and civil-partnership conversion, and consideration of the 2016 equality bill - the primary legislative record of the territory's marriage-equality debate.

A public broadcaster (July 2016): the territory's first same-sex marriage conversion - a couple converted their civil partnership to marriage, keeping their original 2015 wedding date; same-sex marriage became legal after formal assent to the 2016 marriage and civil partnership act.

A public broadcaster (Nov 2005): the elected lower legislative chamber adopted a clause protecting employees from dismissal on grounds of sexual orientation - an amendment to the employment bill, done proactively 'in line with human rights legislation'.

The island's national radio (June 2015): the chief minister announced he believed in same-sex marriage and would bring a bill to scrap prohibitive legislation, discussing it with the senior bishop of the island's established church - at the time, this territory and one constituent jurisdiction of the controlling state were the only parts of that state where LGBT people could not wed.
